title: Grade 10 Mathematics — Heights & Distances + Statistics
description: Applications of Trigonometry (Heights and Distances) and Statistics practice questions
subject: mathematics

questions.question: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point on the ground 30 m away is 30°. The height of the tower is:
The angle of elevation of a point on a wall from the ground at a horizontal distance of 10 m is 45°. The height of that point is:
A ladder 20 m long leans against a vertical wall. If its foot is 10 m from the base of the wall, the angle made with the ground is:
From the top of a cliff 60 m high, the angle of depression of a boat is 30°. The horizontal distance of the boat from the base of the cliff is:
questions.explanation: Angle of depression = 30°. tan 30° = 60/d → d = 60/tan 30° = 60 × √3 = 60√3 m.

questions.question: A vertical pole of height h casts a shadow of length h√3 on the ground. The angle of elevation of the sun is:
Two poles of heights 6 m and 11 m stand on a plane ground. If the distance between their feet is 12 m, the distance between their tops is:
questions.explanation: The vertical difference in heights = 11 − 6 = 5 m. Horizontal distance = 12 m. Distance between tops = √(5² + 12²) = √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13 m.

questions.question: The angle of elevation of a cloud from a point 60 m above a lake is 30° and the angle of depression of the reflection of the cloud is 60°. The height of the cloud from the water surface is:
questions.explanation: Let cloud be at height H above lake, point P is 60 m above lake. Let horizontal distance = d. tan 30° = (H−60)/d and tan 60° = (H+60)/d. Dividing: 3 = (H+60)/(H−60) → 3H−180 = H+60 → H = 120 m.

questions.question: The mean of the data 4, 7, 11, 13, x is 9. The value of x is:
The median of the data 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15 is:
questions.explanation: There are 7 observations. Median = 4th value (in ascending order) = 9.

questions.question: In a frequency distribution, the class with the highest frequency is called:
questions.explanation: The modal class is the class interval that has the highest frequency. The mode of grouped data lies in this class.

questions.question: The sum of the deviations of all observations from their mean is always:
questions.explanation: A fundamental property: the sum of deviations (x − x̄) of all observations from the arithmetic mean is always zero.

questions.question: For a grouped data with class intervals 10–20, 20–30, … the assumed mean (a) is taken at the midpoint of the middle class. If 5 classes start at 10 with width 10, the assumed mean is:
In a grouped frequency distribution, the formula for mode is: Mode = l + [(f₁ − f₀)/(2f₁ − f₀ − f₂)] × h. Here h represents:
questions.explanation: In the mode formula, h is the class size (width of the class interval), l is the lower boundary of the modal class, and f₁, f₀, f₂ are the modal, pre-modal, and post-modal frequencies.

questions.question: The empirical relationship between mean, median, and mode is:
questions.explanation: The empirical formula: Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean. This is approximately true for moderately skewed distributions.
